goal: Increase full-request generated tokens per second for the interactive workload, preserving the source generation length and correctness checks.
completion: One complete infer() execution of the interactive workload: under torch.inference_mode(), a CUDA-synchronized start boundary, prefill of the 256-token GPU-resident input_ids with use_cache=True and logits_to_keep=1 followed by argmax of the first token, an explicit CUDA-synchronized first-token-ready boundary (the source's TTFT point), exactly new_tokens-1=31 KV-cached greedy decode steps, then torch.cat of the generated tokens and a final CUDA-synchronized end boundary. The workload is complete only after that final synchronize; EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit loop, so exactly 32 tokens are produced.
state_protocol: prepare() loads the tokenizer and Qwen3ForCausalLM from request['assets']['qwen3_4b_weights'] (bfloat16, sdpa, eval) onto context['device'], applies the source's numerical policies (TF32 disabled, float32 matmul precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark off, torch.manual_seed(20261020), thread caps) and builds the chat-templated (enable_thinking=False) prompt repeated/truncated to prompt_tokens and replicated to batch, all outside timing. run() is fully self-contained: it creates its own request-local KV cache and generated-token list each invocation, so reset() only restores the RNG seed and is otherwise a no-op; the process group is never destroyed. set_mode('quality') retains per-step logits exactly like the source's capture path, while 'measure'/'profile' keep the source's clean timing path that drops them; execution semantics and work amount are identical across modes.
invariants: Exactly new_tokens=32 greedy tokens are generated; EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit decode loop, so generation length is fixed.

Input is the chat-templated config prompt (apply_chat_template with add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False), encoded without special tokens, repeated and truncated to prompt_tokens=256, replicated to batch=1, resident on the bound CUDA device.

Model is Qwen3ForCausalLM loaded from the frozen local asset revision with dtype=torch.bfloat16 and attn_implementation='sdpa', in eval mode, called with use_cache=True and logits_to_keep=1 on every step.
Numerical policies match common.py:configure: TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark off, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', seed 20261020.
Token selection is argmax over the last-position logits at every step (greedy, deterministic); no sampling randomness affects outputs.
generated_tokens_per_second = batch * new_tokens / end-to-end elapsed time, where the window includes prefill and the first token; it is not decode-only throughput and not TTFT.
TTFT is measured at the source's explicit first-token boundary: the CUDA synchronize immediately after prefill and the first argmax complete; the decode window covers the remaining 31 cached steps.

Correctness observations are the generated token ids (exact integer equality) and the per-step last-token logits for all 32 positions compared at logits_atol=logits_rtol=0.02, matching the source's capture path.
Timing excludes model/tokenizer loading, chat-template tokenization, host input construction, correctness comparisons, warmup/repeats, and profiling; these belong to setup or the harness.
Single process on one bound GPU (no distributed backend); the adapter never initializes a process group and uses context['device'] rather than choosing a physical GPU.
Workload, objective, quality thresholds and asset revision are frozen; batch=1, prompt_tokens=256 and new_tokens=32 must not be changed to improve a score.
assumptions: The prompt text is taken verbatim from the qwen_inference config in the source workloads.json and embedded in the adapter, because the request's workload row carries only sizes; token ids are derived at prepare time with the asset tokenizer exactly as the source does.
The worker's device binding replaces the source's hardcoded device 0: context['device'] is used for cuda.set_device, the input tensor and the model, with rank/world_size taken from context.

Reference fidelity (framework-side reference observations, the source's teacher-forced replay, torch.equal token check and the +1-corruption negative control) is the responsibility of the harness; the adapter supplies the full tokens and per-step logits from the same greedy path in quality mode.

The source's separate capture path (infer(capture=True)) motivates set_mode: full logits are retained in quality mode while measure/profile mode preserves the clean timing path that does not retain them; work amount is identical in both modes.

warmup=2, repeats=5, continuous_steps=2 and the optional torch.profiler diagnostic are statistical harness fields executed by the framework around run(); they are not part of the repeated work unit and are not reimplemented.
The offline (batch=8) row and the held-out long_prompt workload in the source's config are outside this frozen request and are not implemented.

peak_allocated_bytes in metrics() is read after run from torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated on the bound device, relying on the framework's peak-stats reset immediately before its timer, matching the source's sample collection.
No accuracy, convergence or generation-quality claim beyond the source's reference-fidelity checks is made.

implementation_choices: adapter.run reproduces infer() from qwen_inference.py line-for-line in timing structure, including the internal CUDA synchronizations that define the source's start, first-token and end boundaries, because the subphase metrics (ttft_ms, decode_ms) require those internal completion points.

The internal perf_counter_ns windows are returned in result['timing'] and exposed by metrics(); the frozen objective itself is derived from the framework's elapsed_ms over the unchanged full workload.
kernel_optimizer.project.discovery.phase annotates the 'prefill' and 'decode' task phases for discovery; no operator groups or optimization targets are preselected.
set_num_interop_threads is attempted once and skipped if the host process already started inter-op parallel work, since the source sets it before any model work.
unused_source_elements: profile_once/--profile diagnostic (not requested by this invocation)
